prohibitions: Never modify or update Notion pages
guide.summary: Because other customer workspaces will connect, use a public OAuth integration, which Notion says is needed for any workspace. Each customer authorizes through the OAuth flow and picks pages in the page picker. Request only the Read content capability. Titles and content both use Read content endpoints. Discovery of which shared pages exist is not covered by the supplied sources and must be checked before rollout.

findings.detail: Notion documents OAuth integrations for acting on behalf of each user, with a per-user access token. Each user authorizes separately.

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to

findings.title: Use a public integration for customers in any workspace
findings.detail: A scoped integration can only be installed in selected workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Multi-workspace customer access requires a public integration. Installation scope cannot be changed later.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations or workspaces connect (confirmed audience).

evidence.quote: ​ Installation scope Choose Or select 1 or more workspaces when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration .
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. If you later need to make the app available to any workspace, create a new integration.

findings.title: Request the Read content capability
findings.detail: Read content gives access to read existing content. Retrieving a page and its markdown requires read content capabilities on the target page. Titles and content can both be covered by this single capability, with no write capability requested.

evidence.quote: Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve
Requirements Your connection must have read content capabilities on the target page in order to call this endpoint. To update your connection’s capabilities, navigate to the Developer portal , select
​ Errors The connection needs read content capabilities . Missing capabilities return 403 . A missing page or missing access returns 404 .

findings.title: Customers choose which pages to share during authorization
findings.detail: After consent, the user selects which pages the connection can access in the page picker. Access is limited to those pages, so unshared pages return not found.

evidence.quote: 3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.

findings.detail: The OAuth flow exchanges a code for an access token used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user. Do not reuse internal connection or personal tokens.

steps.title: Create a public OAuth integration with the Read content capability
steps.detail: In the Developer portal Connections section, create a new connection as a public integration with a redirect URI, and select only the Read content capability. Do not select Insert or Update content.
steps.doneWhen: A public connection exists with a redirect URI and only the Read content capability enabled.

evidence.quote: your app available to any workspace, create a public integration .
Go to the Developer portal . In the Build section, select Connections . This is also where you create OAuth integrations limited to selected workspaces.
Select Create new connection . Enter the connection name, development workspace, and redirect URIs . Choose Or select 1 or more workspaces , select the workspaces, and choose the capabilities
Read content : This capability gives a connection access to read existing content in a Notion workspace. For example, a connection with only this capability is able to call Retrieve

steps.title: Record the OAuth client ID and secret for the test app
steps.detail: Open the Configuration tab and store the client ID and client secret in a secret manager for the test environment. Do not commit them.
steps.doneWhen: Client ID and client secret are stored in the test app's secret store.

evidence.quote: Open the Configuration tab to find your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret . Use them to implement the OAuth authorization flow .

steps.title: Implement the authorization URL, redirect callback and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL from the Configuration tab, then exchange the returned code at the token endpoint using Basic auth with client ID and secret. Store the access token per customer workspace.
steps.doneWhen: The app builds the authorization URL and exchanges a code for an access token in the test environment.

evidence.quote: 1 The user visits the connection’s authorization URL. Find this URL in the Configuration tab of your connection in the Developer portal.
To set up this step, retrieve the code from the redirect URI.
Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .
Authorization : Basic "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET"

steps.title: Authorize a representative test workspace and select shared test pages
steps.detail: As a representative test user in a test workspace, open the authorization URL, approve the capability prompt, and select two test pages in the page picker, one shared and one unshared.
steps.doneWhen: A token is issued for the test workspace and the callback stores it, with the test pages selected.

evidence.quote: 2 Notion presents a prompt describing the connection’s capabilities — what it will be able to do in the user’s workspace.
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.
4 After the user approves, Notion redirects them to your redirect URI with a temporary authorization code.
5 Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.

steps.detail: Call the page retrieval endpoint with the title filter using the OAuth token for the shared test page. Expected: 200 with the title property. Boundary check: call the same endpoint for the unshared page and confirm it returns 404, and confirm no request was a write.
steps.doneWhen: The shared page returns its title and the unshared page returns 404 with no write request sent.
